record.prBody:
## GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini, GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1 mini snapshots shut down Jan 14, 2027; migrate to gpt-6-luna [Verified]

### Change

Changed model in functions/src/index.ts from gpt-4o-2024-08-06 to gpt-6-luna. No other code or dependency changes.

Files touched:
- `functions/src/index.ts`
- `tsconfig.app.tsbuildinfo`
- `tsconfig.node.tsbuildinfo`

### Why

gpt-4o-2024-08-06 shuts down 2027-01-14; calls would fail after that.

> On October 14, 2026, we notified developers using certain GPT-4 series models of their deprecation and removal from the API on January 14, 2027.

Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck | pass | pass | 0 |
| build | pass | pass | 0 |
| model-pin | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- model-pin, added by the agent: `grep -q 'gpt-6-luna' functions/src/index.ts && ! grep -q 'gpt-4' functions/src/index.ts` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider tool calls recorded by the harness:
- `openai__openai_check_request`: pass

The agent's validator claims (not proof; graded against the recorded calls):
- openai_check_request: pass (chat.completions with gpt-6-luna: no unknown or deprecated params, model active)

Test of this change: `model-pin`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- The model-pin check is a grep, not a mocked call.
- openai@4.77.3 beta.chat.completions.parse and zodResponseFormat with gpt-6-luna were not run live. Only the typecheck and build passed.
- Whether the SDK version supports gpt-6-luna structured outputs was not checked.

### Behaviour changes

- Resume extraction now runs on gpt-6-luna. Output quality, latency and cost may differ, so check it on real resumes.
- The replacement may be a reasoning model, which is untested here. No temperature or max_tokens is set, so no parameter changes were needed.

---

preparation.reasoning: The root project has no codegen or prepare/postinstall hooks, and the build (tsc -b && vite build) only needs the installed dependencies. The functions/ subfolder is a separate project, but the checks run from the root and the root tsconfig likely does not include it. The README mentions a .env file, but the vite config does not need one to load or build, and any VITE_ variables are read at runtime. Nothing environmental is required.

review.summary: The model-string swap in functions/src/index.ts:51 is the only call site, and it is updated. Three things hold this back from 'verified'. First, the PR commits two unrelated generated tsbuildinfo files. Second, none of the checks exercise a live structured-output call. Third, I could not confirm from the quoted source that 'gpt-6-luna' is the named replacement or that it supports json_schema structured outputs through beta.chat.completions.parse. Typecheck and build pass on any string literal, and model-pin only proves the old ID is gone. So the 'verified' grade overstates what was tested.

concerns.issue: The model is changed from the dated snapshot 'gpt-4o-2024-08-06' to 'gpt-6-luna'. The quoted deprecation line does not name the replacement, and I can't confirm this model ID or that it supports zodResponseFormat / json_schema structured outputs. Check the deprecations page's replacement table and the model's docs.

The swap may change behaviour beyond the forced migration: extraction quality, latency, cost, and how missing fields are handled. The schema has required string fields (email, phone, education), and the prompt says to return null for missing fields. A newer model may react differently to that conflict. Also, the new pin is an alias rather than a dated snapshot, so future silent model changes become possible.

No check makes a real call through openai.beta.chat.completions.parse. A rejected model name or unsupported response_format would only appear at runtime. The function's catch block turns every error into a generic 'internal' HttpsError, so the failure would be hard to diagnose from the client.
This is an unrelated build artifact (along with tsconfig.node.tsbuildinfo) committed by the build check. It should be removed from the PR and probably added to .gitignore.

checkFirst: Confirm on developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations that gpt-6-luna is the recommended replacement for gpt-4o-2024-08-06, and that it supports Structured Outputs via json_schema / beta.chat.completions.parse with the installed openai SDK version.
Run extractStructuredData once against the live API with a sample resume and verify message.parsed is populated.
Drop tsconfig.app.tsbuildinfo and tsconfig.node.tsbuildinfo from the PR.
Downgrade the grade to needs-review until a live call is verified.

source.quote: * require Node.js 22 and codify version support ([#2026](https://github.com/openai/openai-node/issues/2026))

tasks.reasoning: The Cloud Functions package pins openai 4.77.3 (functions/yarn.lock), which falls in the <7.0.0 range of this major. This is not a hard break today: 4.x keeps working until the API rejects it. It is a pending major upgrade, and 7.0.0 requires Node.js 22. The migration agent should check the Node runtime declared in functions/package.json engines and the firebase.json runtime, and raise it to 22 if needed. It should also move beta.chat.completions.parse to chat.completions.parse and confirm zodResponseFormat and zod compatibility. The 7.43/7.44 Live Decisions type changes do not touch this repo, which does not use Live Decisions. This is optional and low urgency; the effective date is the release date, not a shutdown.

callSites.why: Uses beta.chat.completions.parse from openai 4.77.3. Later majors moved parse out of the beta namespace (chat.completions.parse), so this call must be updated when moving to 7.x.
zodResponseFormat (openai/helpers/zod) is used. Its import path and the supported zod version should be verified against openai 7.x.

## openai (npm) 7.0.0 requires Node.js 22 [Verified]

### Change

Upgraded functions/ openai 4.77.3 to ^7.0.0 (yarn, lockfile updated), moved beta.chat.completions.parse to chat.completions.parse, and raised functions engines.node from 18 to 22. Typecheck in functions/ passes with zodResponseFormat and zod 3.x.

Files touched:
- `functions/package.json`
- `functions/src/index.ts`
- `functions/yarn.lock`
- `tsconfig.app.tsbuildinfo`
- `tsconfig.node.tsbuildinfo`

### Why

openai 7.0.0 requires Node.js 22, and the beta.chat namespace no longer exists in the newer SDK, so the call had to move.

> * require Node.js 22 and codify version support ([#2026](https://github.com/openai/openai-node/issues/2026))

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/openai-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck | pass | pass | 0 |
| build | pass | pass | 0 |
| openai7-proof | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- openai7-proof, added by the agent: `export VITE_FIREBASE_API_KEY='placeholder' VITE_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN='placeholder.firebaseapp.com' VITE_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID='placeholder' VITE_FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET='placeholder.appspot.com' VITE_FIREBASE_MESSAGING_SENDER_ID='placeholder' VITE_FIREBASE_APP_ID='placeholder' VITE_OPENAI_API_KEY='placeholder'; cd functions && cat > /tmp/t.mjs <<'EOF'
import fs from 'fs';
const s=fs.readFileSync('src/index.ts','utf8');
const p=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('package.json','utf8'));
if(s.includes('openai.beta.chat')||!s.includes('openai.chat.completions.parse'))process.exit(1);
if(p.engines.node!=='22'||!/\^7/.test(p.dependencies.openai))process.exit(1);
EOF
node /tmp/t.mjs && npx tsc --noEmit` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Prepared before the baseline:
- Checks ran with placeholder env: VITE_FIREBASE_API_KEY, VITE_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN, VITE_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID, VITE_FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET, VITE_FIREBASE_MESSAGING_SENDER_ID, VITE_FIREBASE_APP_ID, VITE_OPENAI_API_KEY.

Test of this change: `openai7-proof`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- The proof test is a source and package.json check plus tsc, not a mocked-client test.
- firebase.json has no runtime setting, so the deployed runtime follows engines (22); not verified that Firebase accepts it.
- Model gpt-4o-2024-08-06 was left unchanged; its retirement is out of scope here.
- Runtime parse behaviour with zod 3.x on openai 7 was not exercised.
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- Cloud Functions runtime moves to Node 22.
- Real response parsing was not exercised; only types were checked.

The functions/ subproject is not part of the root checks (root tsc uses the root tsconfig). The README says a .env is needed, so I supply placeholder Firebase/OpenAI env vars in case they are read at load or build time. No steps are needed.

review.summary: The SDK migration looks correct. The only named call site is at functions/src/index.ts:50, and it moves from `beta.chat.completions.parse` to `chat.completions.parse`. `zodResponseFormat` from `openai/helpers/zod` is unchanged, and typecheck and build pass against the resolved openai 7.49.0. The engines bump to Node 22 is what this change forces. On Firebase it also moves the deployed Cloud Function to the nodejs22 runtime, and no check exercises that deploy. Nothing calls OpenAI live, so the parse/zod path is proven by types only. The PR also commits two unrelated root-level tsbuildinfo artifacts. 'Verified' fits the compile-level checks but overstates confidence about the runtime and deploy change.

concerns.issue: Changing engines.node from 18 to 22 makes Firebase deploy the function on the nodejs22 runtime. This is a production runtime change. No check covers a deploy or emulator run. Whether firebase-functions ^6.0.1, firebase-admin ^12.6.0 and the project's firebase-tools version support Node 22 deployment is not shown here. Local and CI environments running Node 18/20 may also fail to install openai 7 if its engines field is enforced.

Line 50 now calls `openai.chat.completions.parse`, and `.message.parsed` is read at around line 66. Only typecheck confirms that the parse semantics and the zod helper behave as before in 7.x. The schema uses `.optional()` fields, and strict structured outputs has historically required optional fields to be nullable or rejected them. A live call or mocked request would be needed to confirm `zodResponseFormat` still accepts this schema without throwing at runtime.

`^7.0.0` resolved to 7.49.0, well past the version the changelog entry covers. I could not confirm this version or whether it declares a zod peer range compatible with zod ^3.24.1. Check node_modules/openai/package.json (peerDependencies, engines) or the openai-node CHANGELOG between 7.0.0 and 7.49.0 for further breaking changes.

tsconfig.app.tsbuildinfo and tsconfig.node.tsbuildinfo are new build artifacts at the repo root. They are unrelated to the migration and were probably produced by the frontend build check. They should be removed from the PR and likely gitignored.

TypeScript stays at ^4.9.0 (4.9.5 locked). It compiled, but openai 7 may officially require a newer minimum TypeScript version. Confirm in the SDK README or package.json so that future type changes don't break silently.

checkFirst: Confirm the Firebase project and firebase-tools version support the nodejs22 runtime, and run `firebase emulators:start --only functions` or a staging deploy on Node 22.
Exercise extractStructuredData once against the real API, or a recorded response, to confirm `chat.completions.parse` with zodResponseFormat and the optional fields still returns `parsed`.
Check what the openai7-proof check actually asserts.
Drop the stray tsconfig.*.tsbuildinfo files from the PR.

borodinka/hire-wise:openai:npm-7-0-0: The Cloud Functions package pins openai 4.77.3 (functions/yarn.lock), which falls in the <7.0.0 range of this major. This is not a hard break today: 4.x keeps working until the API rejects it. It is a pending major upgrade, and 7.0.0 requires Node.js 22. The migration agent should check the Node runtime declared in functions/package.json engines and the firebase.json runtime, and raise it to 22 if needed. It should also move beta.chat.completions.parse to chat.completions.parse and confirm zodResponseFormat and zod compatibility. The 7.43/7.44 Live Decisions type changes do not touch this repo, which does not use Live Decisions. This is optional and low urgency; the effective date is the release date, not a shutdown.
